label: prf:bar-self-dual-confinement-band
title: Proof of bar self dual confinement band
html:
Proof. Proof of bar self dual confinement band

Proof. The fixed point of \iota on \mathbb{R}_{>0} is q = 1, lying in \mathcal{B}. For a > 0, the interval (a, 1/a) is \iota-invariant if and only if a < 1. Among intervals (a, 1/a) contained in \mathbb{R}_{>0} \setminus \{1/\varphi^2, \varphi^2\}, the maximal one is (1/\varphi^2, \varphi^2). Any larger choice (a, 1/a) with a < 1/\varphi^2 contains the node 1/\varphi^2. Hence \mathcal{B} is maximal. \square

The interval \mathcal{B} = (1/\varphi^2, \varphi^2) unifies three disjoint phase regimes into a single bar-symmetric structure:

Side q regime Sub-band Phase Order parameter
sub-classical q < 1/\varphi^2 below \mathcal{B} low-density deconfined (QGP) \Delta(\mathcal{E}_q) > 0
classical band q \in \mathcal{B} inside \mathcal{B} confined hadronic \Delta(\mathcal{E}_q) < 0
super-classical q > \varphi^2 above \mathcal{B} high-density deconfined (CFL/strangelet limit) \Delta(\mathcal{E}_{1/q}) > 0

Both deconfined regimes are governed by the same algebraic threshold s^2 - s - 1 = 0, applied directly on the super-classical side and via \iota on the sub-classical side.

Our universe sits at q_0 \approx 1.1100 \in \mathcal{B}, with margins

  d_-(q_0)  :=  q_0 - 1/\varphi^2 \approx 0.728,
  \qquad
  d_+(q_0)  :=  \varphi^2 - q_0 \approx 1.508.

The bar-image \iota(q_0) = 1/q_0 \approx 0.901 also lies in \mathcal{B}, with margins

  d_-\bigl(\iota(q_0)\bigr) \approx 0.519,
  \qquad
  d_+\bigl(\iota(q_0)\bigr) \approx 1.717.

The pair (q_0, \iota(q_0)) defines a bar-orbit in \mathcal{B}. Confinement statements holding at q_0 automatically hold at \iota(q_0). We state any phase-boundary argument once for \mathcal{B} and apply it to both endpoints by bar symmetry.
